column1: # comment: "Plan \u27c2 execution de-conflation alignments to P-Plan, PROV-O, schema.org HowTo/Recipe, OPMW, OBI, BPMN, RO-Crate, the workflow engines Airflow / CWL / WDL / Temporal / Nextflow, and openEHR Task Planning (PROC). gmeow:Procedure is a logic:Plan; every engine surface is a lossy by-reference lowering of that canonical process model (Principle 5). openEHR Task Planning is the higher-fidelity target \u2014 it carries loops and guarded branching \u2014 and its distinctive DLM constructs are subsumed natively (currency \u2192 logic:FreshnessGuard's logic:freshnessHorizon age axis AND time_window \u2192 its logic:freshnessWindow explicit valid-time-interval axis \u2014 both orthogonal axes of one guard, manual-notification \u2192 logic:NotificationWaitSchema, ISM linkage \u2192 logic:instantiatesPlan)."

column6: comment
BPMN sequenceFlow; GMEOW ControlFlow is a reified relator with optional guard.
P-Plan precededBy is a direct property between steps; GMEOW ControlFlow is a reified relator.
BPMN dataAssociation; GMEOW DataFlow is a reified relator carrying the flowing entity.
OBI planned process (OBI:0000011); GMEOW Execution is the event occurrence.
OPMW WorkflowExecution; GMEOW Execution is the execution side of the de-conflation.
P-Plan Activity is the execution of a Step; GMEOW Execution is the event that enacts a Procedure or Step.
PROV-O Activity; GMEOW Execution is the event occurrence that enacts a plan.
RO-Crate Workflow-Run CreateAction; GMEOW Execution is the event that enacts a procedure.
OBI protocol (OBI:0000272); GMEOW Procedure generalises this to all prescriptive specs.
OPMW WorkflowTemplate; GMEOW Procedure is the plan side of the de-conflation.
P-Plan Plan; GMEOW Procedure is broader (includes recipes, CI, business processes).
PROV-O Plan; GMEOW Procedure is typed as InformationObject and carries step structure.
schema.org HowTo; GMEOW Procedure is broader (includes protocols, CI, business processes).
schema.org Recipe is a Procedure of type recipe.

Apache Airflow DAG (by reference, no canonical RDF): a procedure is a DAG of tasks. Lossy lowering — Airflow forbids cycles (a logic:Iteration loop must unroll or error) and has no per-outcome compensation (omitted).
Workflow Description Language (WDL) workflow (by reference, no canonical RDF): a procedure is a WDL workflow of calls. Lossy lowering of the canonical plan.

openEHR Task Planning TASK_PLAN / SUB_PLAN (by reference): a constituent sub-procedure (gmeow:hasSubProcedure) is an openEHR task plan nested under a work plan. The sub-plan nesting round-trips; the same concurrency / compensation drops as the work-plan bridge apply.

openEHR Task Planning WORK_PLAN (by reference, no canonical RDF): a top-level procedure is an openEHR work plan. Higher fidelity than the acyclic engines — TP-VML/DLM carries loops and guarded branching, so a logic:Iteration or logic:Choice in the plan projects faithfully rather than unrolling. Lossy only where TP-VML lacks logic:'s concurrency-serializability and per-outcome compensation.

Temporal Workflow (by reference, no canonical RDF): a procedure is a Temporal workflow definition. Temporal DOES express loops and compensation (saga) imperatively, so the lowering is closer for control flow but is a code surface, not a declarative spec — carried by reference only.

Common Workflow Language Workflow (by reference, no stable RDF term IRIs): a procedure is a CWL workflow. Lossy — CWL is acyclic dataflow (a logic:Iteration loop must unroll) and carries no compensation (omitted).

Nextflow workflow (by reference, no canonical RDF): a procedure is a Nextflow dataflow workflow of processes. Lossy — Nextflow concurrency is channel-implicit (a logic:ConcurrentComposition serializes in the spec view) and there is no compensation primitive (omitted).
OPMW WorkflowTemplateProcess; GMEOW ProcedureStep is the atomic step in a plan.
P-Plan Step; GMEOW ProcedureStep adds stepType values and subprocess composition.
schema.org HowToStep; GMEOW ProcedureStep adds control-flow and data-flow relators.
Apache Airflow Task (by reference): a procedure step is an Airflow task node in the DAG.
Workflow Description Language (WDL) task (by reference): a procedure step is a WDL task.

openEHR Task Planning TASK / TASK_ACTION (by reference): a procedure step is an openEHR task. A DLM-gated task maps to a guarded logic:Choice step (preserved, not unrolled); a manual-notification task maps to logic:NotificationWaitSchema (subsumed natively); a DLM currency-guarded task input maps to logic:FreshnessGuard (subsumed natively) — BOTH its axes: `currency` (max age) to logic:freshnessHorizon and `time_window` (an explicit valid-time interval) to logic:freshnessWindow / logic:freshnessWindowStart / logic:freshnessWindowEnd.
Temporal Activity (by reference): a procedure step is a Temporal activity invoked by the workflow.
Common Workflow Language WorkflowStep (by reference): a procedure step is a CWL workflow step.
Nextflow process (by reference): a procedure step is a Nextflow process node consuming/producing channels.

An if-then guard on a gmeow:ControlFlow edge realizes the canonical binary choice combinator logic:Choice (the guarded then-arm vs. the alternative). Structural, not equivalent: the guard VALUE marks which combinator the reified edge realizes, it is not the combinator class. The implicit else / default arm corresponds to logic:Fallback (try the guarded arm, else the default).

A loop-back guard on a gmeow:ControlFlow edge realizes the canonical iteration combinator logic:Iteration (logic:iterationBody gated by logic:iterationCondition). Structural, not equivalent. A loop is a back-edge in the flow graph, so a procedure carrying a loop guard is outside the acyclic DAG fragment the certifier accepts.

A parallel split/join guard on a gmeow:ControlFlow edge realizes the canonical concurrent-composition combinator logic:ConcurrentComposition (two co-equal legs run concurrently). Structural, not equivalent.

An n-way switch guard on a gmeow:ControlFlow edge realizes the canonical choice combinator logic:Choice. logic:Choice is BINARY (logic:leftOperand / logic:rightOperand), so an n-way switch corresponds to a right-nested cascade of binary logic:Choice nodes; the single canonical combinator target is logic:Choice. Structural, not equivalent. The implicit default case corresponds to logic:Fallback.
schema.org step — the steps of a HowTo.
P-Plan Input variable; GMEOW stepInput is a property pointing to any entity.
PROV-O used — an activity consumes an entity; GMEOW stepInput is the plan-level consumption.
schema.org supply — a consumable input to a HowToStep.
schema.org tool — a tool used in a HowToStep.
P-Plan Output variable; GMEOW stepOutput is a property pointing to any entity.
PROV-O wasGeneratedBy — an entity is produced by an activity; GMEOW stepOutput is the plan-level production.
schema.org result — the output of a HowTo.
BPMN gateway; GMEOW stepTypeBranch is a value on a ProcedureStep.
